From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>

Subject: Follow-up: model fit + next steps from today

Hi Samir / Ruchi,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great discussion on the bursty inference patterns you see for your summarization pipeline and the latency SLOs you need for interactive review (p95 < 250ms at 4k context). A quick recap and proposed next steps: 

- Summary of notes:
  - Primary workload: user-facing doc summarization with high variability in sequence length (512–4096 tokens).
  - Target SLOs: p95 latency ~<250ms, throughput ~200 TPS for peak windows.
  - Success metric: qualitative parity with current vendor on ROUGE/QA prompts + 30% reduction in unit token cost.

- Proposed evaluation plan:
  1) Share prompt set + sample traces (you mentioned you can export the prompt/trace JSON).
  2) Redwood will run 2 benchmark passes: (a) recommended dense model baseline; (b) quantized 4-bit variant to measure cost/latency tradeoffs.
  3) Deliver Redwood-verified performance profiles (TPS, latency percentiles, token cost estimates) and a short quality summary (ROUGE / QA pass rate).

Next steps for this week:
- Samir: share prompt_set_v1 + sample traces (you said by Friday).
- Me/Dylan: run initial bench and share Redwood-verified report and suggested models.

I’m cc'ing Dylan to loop him in on the traces (he’ll run the bench job). If it helps, I can also loop in Marissa — she owns the benchmark reports and can share the Redwood-verified perf profiles.

Thanks,
Alex Martinez

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acme.ai>
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2026 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Redwood benchmark: initial results + recommended models

Hi Samir, Alex, Dylan —

We completed the first-pass benchmark against the prompt_set_v1 you provided. High-level summary below; full Redwood-verified report is attached and the interactive dashboard is linked.

High-level findings:
- Recommended primary model: RW-OPT-13B (dense) — best balance of quality and latency for your reviewer workload.
- Cost/latency tradeoff candidate: RW-OPT-13B (4-bit quantized) — ~28% token-cost reduction with a small quality delta.

Redwood-verified performance profile (simulated reviewer workload, 4k max context):
- RW-OPT-13B (dense): peak TPS (batched) = 220 TPS; p50 = 48ms; p90 = 140ms; p95 = 210ms.
- RW-OPT-13B (4-bit): peak TPS (batched) = 260 TPS; p50 = 42ms; p90 = 120ms; p95 = 180ms.
- RW-XYZ-7B (dense): peak TPS = 340 TPS; p95 = 320ms (quality gap on long-context prompts).

Quality checks (sampled):
- RW-OPT-13B (dense): ROUGE-L = 0.72; QA pass rate = 91%.
- RW-OPT-13B (4-bit): ROUGE-L = 0.70; QA pass rate = 89% (delta within acceptable bounds per our threshold but note a few edge cases on long-context coherence).

Attachments + links:
- Attached: redwood_benchmark_report_v2.pdf (full perf tables, methodology, and cost modeling).
- Dashboard: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/acme-ai-model-fit-2026
- HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.com/deal/ACME-2026-05

Notes / recommendations:
- For interactive reviewer SLOs, we recommend RW-OPT-13B (4-bit) as a cost-optimized default with canary rollout to capture any edge-case regressions.
- If you need stricter p95 headroom, consider RW-OPT-13B dense pinned on dedicated capacity for predictable latency.
- We simulated KV cache hit rates at ~65% per your traces; if your actual cache hits are higher, expect improved p95.

Next steps:
- If you want, we can run a second pass with your prefix-caching config toggled and a larger QA sample (we quoted this in the report).
- Happy to set up a 30-min walkthrough on Monday to go over the dashboard and recommended rollout plan.

Thanks — attaching the report and the prompt set we ran.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Product Benchmarks Lead | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
